title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
content_md: TL;DR: Our analysis shows attackers are now enumerating or pulling data within 15 minutes of getting into an environment, and the tools that should have caught them were not effective. We will discuss three common attack patterns in which we observed this behavior. Catching these incidents takes detection built on data and behavior. Stopping them takes an autonomous response. We cover both of these topics. In March, a developer installed GitHub Desktop, signed in, and stopped using it the same day. The OAuth token it created sat in the Mac's keychain for 95 days. On June 19, someone else started using it. The token pulled 76 repositories in about 15 seconds through residential proxies in more than two dozen European cities. GitHub raised no alert because nothing in GitHub watches how tokens are used. The Exaforce platform flagged it within five minutes and had it triaged within 10 minutes. Our MDR analysts confirmed the exfiltration and notified the customer minutes after the detection fired. But by the time any action was taken, the attacker had exfiltrated data from 472 of the 638 repos. This case shows both halves of the problem. Without anomaly detection, nobody would have known the token was in use. With proper detection in place, containment would still have required human approval, giving the attacker sufficient time to exfiltrate data.
